# Lock In Design System

> Cross-platform design system (React for web, React Native for iOS/Android) for personal projects: tournament apps, web games, dashboards, web stores. WCAG 2.1 AA, light and dark modes, project themes. Every token and component is available as structured JSON for AI agents.

## Connect (preferred: MCP)
- MCP over HTTP: POST {origin}/mcp (reading needs no key; editors send `Authorization: Bearer <api key>`)
- MCP over stdio (local): `npx tsx apps/server/src/stdio.ts`
- Tools: search_design_system, list_components, get_component, get_tokens, get_token, check_contrast, list_icons, list_docs, get_doc, get_changelog (+ update_component, update_token, update_doc for editors)
- Resources: ds://overview, ds://tokens/{light|dark}, ds://components/{slug}, ds://docs/{slug}

## REST (same data)
- GET /api/components, /api/components/{slug}
- GET /api/tokens?prefix=color.text, /api/tokens/{name}
- GET /api/search?q=..., /api/contrast?fg=..&bg=..&mode=dark
- GET /api/docs, /api/docs/{slug}

## Rules for building UI with Lock In
1. Use a Lock In component when one fits; read its spec (get_component) and follow props, accessibility and usage do/don't exactly.
2. Style custom UI with semantic tokens only (color.text.*, color.background.*, color.surface.*, color.border.*, color.intent.*, color.status.*, space.*, typography.*). Never hard-code hex values or use base palette tokens like color.blue.600.
3. Web: CSS variables `--ds-<token-path-with-dashes>`. Native: `const { t } = useTheme(); t.color.text.primary`.
4. Every form control needs a visible label; never convey meaning by color alone; keep focus visible; touch targets ≥ 44px.
5. Check any new color pairing with check_contrast (4.5:1 text, 3:1 UI).

## Components
Button, Icon, Link, Checkbox, RadioGroup (radio-button), Toggle, InputField, Search, Select, Dropdown, Tabs, Tag, Modal, DataTable
